questions.stem: What is the universal first step for almost any mobile device problem?

choices.text: Restart (turn it off and on again)

questions.explanation: A simple restart clears temporary files and resolves a huge number of glitches; it's the universal first step for almost any mobile problem.
questions.trap: A factory reset wipes everything and is a last resort, not the first thing to try.

questions.stem: An app crashes repeatedly. What is the correct order of escalation to fix it?

choices.text: Factory reset, then reinstall the OS, then restart
Replace the phone, then call the carrier
Force close the app, restart the phone, update the app, then reinstall the app
Clear the SIM card, then re-pair Bluetooth

questions.explanation: The sequence is: force close the app, restart the phone, check for an app update, and as a last resort uninstall/reinstall the app.
questions.trap: Jumping straight to a factory reset or replacing the phone skips the cheap, fast fixes that usually work.

questions.stem: An app fails to install or update. Which checklist item is NOT one of the recommended things to verify?

choices.text: A valid payment method on file

questions.explanation: For install/update failures, check storage, connectivity, a valid payment method (even free apps may require one), and, on work devices, MDM policies. Screen brightness is irrelevant.
questions.trap: Brightness has nothing to do with installs; the real culprits are storage, connectivity, payment method, or MDM blocks.

questions.stem: On a corporate (work) device, an app install is being blocked even though storage and connectivity are fine. What is the likely cause?

choices.text: Device management (MDM) policies are blocking the installation
The phone is in airplane mode permanently

questions.explanation: On a work device, the MDM may be blocking the installation by policy - check device-management policies.
questions.trap: A dirty screen protector and a broken accelerometer have nothing to do with an install being policy-blocked.

questions.stem: A phone suffers frequent random reboots. After confirming the OS and all apps are fully updated, what does the review say frequent random reboots often indicate?

choices.text: A normal software behavior requiring no action
A hardware failure that may require replacing the device

questions.explanation: After ruling out software bugs by updating the OS and apps, frequent random reboots often point to a hardware failure that may require device replacement.
questions.trap: A full browser cache or wrong time zone does not cause repeated spontaneous reboots.

questions.stem: Which is identified as the number-one cause of poor battery life on a phone?

choices.text: A weak cellular signal that makes the phone constantly hunt for bars

questions.explanation: A weak cellular signal is the number-one battery drain because the phone constantly hunts for bars. In a no-service area, switch to airplane mode.
questions.trap: Stored photos and wallpaper choice are not significant battery drains compared to a radio searching for signal.

questions.stem: A user is in an area with no cellular service and wants to preserve battery. What is the recommended action?
questions.explanation: In a no-service area, switching to airplane mode stops the phone from draining the battery hunting for a signal.
questions.trap: Leaving radios like GPS and Bluetooth on (and a bright screen) drains the battery faster, the opposite of the goal.

questions.stem: Bluetooth won't connect on a phone. After confirming the radio is enabled, what is the recommended next step?

choices.text: Toggle the radio off and on again; if that fails, restart the device

questions.explanation: For connectivity issues (Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, NFC), make sure the radio is enabled, then toggle it off and on; if that fails, restart the device.
questions.trap: A factory reset is far too drastic as an early step for a simple radio connectivity glitch.

questions.stem: A phone's screen won't auto-rotate between portrait and landscape. What is the most common simple cause?

choices.text: Rotation lock is accidentally enabled in the quick settings
The OS needs a full reinstall

questions.explanation: Auto-rotate failures almost always come down to the rotation lock being accidentally enabled - check the quick settings panel.
questions.trap: Accelerometer hardware failure is possible but rare; check the simple software lock first.

questions.stem: An iPhone app is frozen and unresponsive. How do you force close it?

choices.text: Hold the power button until it reboots
Put the phone in airplane mode
Swipe the app off the screen in the app switcher

questions.explanation: On an iPhone you force close an app by swiping it off the screen in the app switcher. (On Android you use Force Stop in app settings.)
questions.trap: Deleting the app removes it entirely; force-closing just stops the frozen instance so you can reopen it.
